study: Motteram et al. 2016, ReflectED metacognition (Rosendale) EEF efficacy trial, Year-5 pupils, ~1-year post (ERIC ED581262)
eval_evidence: EEF efficacy trial with an independent evaluation team (University of Manchester); report header lists 'Independent evaluators:' (Manchester) distinct from the developer, Rosendale Primary School.
developer_evidence: The developer delivered the PD: 'Rosendale Primary School trained teachers from 30 schools'; 'A team of mentors from Rosendale Primary School trained and supported the primary schools'; report notes 'close involvement of the original developer in the delivery of the programme.'
cascade_evidence: Rosendale (the developer) trained the intervention teachers directly via its own mentor team and launch/training days; one hop developer->teacher, no train-the-trainer intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: 'There were two arms: intervention (ReflectED) and control (business as usual)'; controls continued normal practice.
coaching_evidence: Five training days plus an assigned Rosendale school mentor, weekly emailed reminders/tips, and online support from the London Connected Learning Centre; periodic/light mentor support rather than recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Metacognition lessons are delivered by the trained classroom teachers as part of regular instruction ('these lessons teach children specific metacognitive strategies', taught by the teacher); no separate tutoring/pull-out/added-minutes dose to pupils.
maturity_evidence: Efficacy trial; teachers newly trained in 2014 (launch summer 2014), with the cohort taught and post-tested at the end of one academic year (June 2015) -> first implementation year for these teachers.
